Kill Switch

Store pageSource code

Kill Switch chops your signal in a rhythm, like the momentary kill switch some guitars have: while the plugin is on, a looping pattern lets the sound through or cuts it, in time with the tempo you set. Bypassed, your signal is clean.

You pick one of 10 patterns (from a plain chop to a machine gun) or write your own, set the tempo and the speed, and then use Depth and Edge to decide how deep and how hard the cuts are. It is one mono audio effect, with a footswitch on the plugin that is also its bypass.

01

Quick start

You need a pedalboard with an audio input and an output, and a guitar (or any sound) going through it.

  1. Add Kill Switch to your pedalboard and connect it between your guitar input and the rest of the chain (or between the amp and the output). It has one audio input and one audio output.
  2. Turn it on. The plugin starts on (the red light over the footswitch is lit and the label says On): play a note and it is chopped at once. Click the footswitch to bypass it: the sound is clean again.

  3. Choose a pattern. Use the arrows on each side of its name. The squares under the name show the pattern: a lit square lets the signal through, a dark one cuts it.

  4. Set the tempo with − and + (hold one to go on), and pick the speed (½x, 1x, 2x, 4x): the same pattern at half, normal, double or four times its speed, without touching the tempo.

  5. Shape the cut. Depth is how much of the signal a cut removes (100% is silence) and Edge is how long it takes to close and open (short is a hard, percussive chop; long is a soft swell).

  6. Put it under your foot. Assign the plugin's footswitch (its Bypass) to a device footswitch, in Momentary mode if you want the effect on only while you hold it, as with the switch on a guitar (section 5).

Every pattern starts the moment you switch the plugin on

Whenever the plugin goes from bypassed to on, the pattern starts again from its first step. The ten built-in patterns all begin with a cut, as if you had pressed the kill switch right then (in your own pattern, the first step is whatever you set). Press the footswitch in time with the beat and the chops fall where you want them.

02

The plugin on the pedalboard

Item What it does
Pattern: the arrows and the name Choose the pattern (section 3). The arrows go round: after the last pattern comes the first, and the last one is Custom, the pattern you write.
The sixteen squares The pattern. A bright red square lets the signal through, a dark one cuts it, and a darker red one is the middle level (only in your own patterns). A pattern shorter than sixteen steps is repeated; the first run is bright and the repetitions are dimmer, so you can see where it starts again. The squares go dim when the plugin is bypassed.
Edit pattern Opens the settings page: everything on the plugin with more room, the editor of your own pattern and the buttons that assign each control to a device control (section 4).
Tempo: − and + The speed of the pattern, from 40 to 240 BPM. Hold a button to keep going.
Speed ½x, 1x, 2x or 4x: multiplies the speed of the pattern without changing the tempo.
Depth From 0% to 100%: how much of the signal a cut removes. 100% is silence; lower values only dip the level, like a tremolo with sharp edges.
Edge From 0.1 ms to 20 ms, on a logarithmic scale: how long a cut takes to close and to open again.
The footswitch and its light The bypass of the plugin. The ring and the light above it are red while the effect is on, and the label at the top says On or Bypassed.
Audio jacks In on the left, Out on the right.

All five controls (and the bypass) can be assigned to a device control: see section 5.

03

The patterns

Each pattern is a loop of steps. In every step the signal is either let through or cut; the plugin goes from one step to the next in time with the tempo, and from the last step back to the first. The grids show every pattern as sixteen steps (the shorter ones repeat): a coloured square lets the signal through and a grey one cuts it.

12345678910111213141516
Chop 8ths
Chop 16ths
Triplet chop
Machine gun
Syncopated 3-3-2
Gallop

Generic grooves

Six patterns that fit any style. Chop 8ths and Chop 16ths are the plain on-off chop at those note values, Triplet chop does it in triplets, Machine gun is the same at thirty-second notes, Syncopated 3-3-2 is the Latin-flavoured grouping of eight steps (three, three and two) and Gallop is a short-short-long figure of four.

Steps per beat: Chop 8ths 2 · Chop 16ths 4 · Triplet chop 3 · Machine gun 8 · Syncopated 3-3-2 2 · Gallop 4

12345678910111213141516
Morello solo chop
Morello toggle solo
Greenwood chunk
Buckethead burst

Inspired by guitarists famous for the kill switch

Four longer, busier patterns named after players known for the kill switch. The rhythms are our approximation, not a transcription of anyone's playing: use them as a starting point and change the tempo, the speed, the depth and the edge until it fits your song.

Steps per beat: Morello solo chop 4 · Morello toggle solo 4 · Greenwood chunk 2 · Buckethead burst 8

The tempo says how many beats there are in a minute, and every pattern has its own number of steps per beat (the line under each grid), so the length of a step is 60 / (tempo × steps per beat × speed) seconds. At 120 BPM, Chop 8ths has a step of 250 ms and Machine gun a step of 62.5 ms.

The tempo is the plugin's own

Kill Switch does not follow the tempo of the pedalboard or of a MIDI clock: set the tempo here, or assign it to a knob or to an expression pedal.

04

Your own pattern

The eleventh pattern, Custom, is yours. Click Edit pattern on the plugin (or open its settings with the gear icon). The settings page has everything the plugin has, with more room, and its first page is where you play and write:

  • The choice: every pattern to pick with one tap, and a Preview of its steps (it only shows: it is not a control). Choosing Custom opens the editor right there, under the preview.
  • Tempo and feel, beside it: the tempo (with its buttons and a slider), Speed, Depth and Edge.
  • In the top bar, on every page: On / Bypassed, the footswitch of the plugin.

On a small screen there is no room for all of it on one page: the editor then has a page of its own, and a button under the list, Edit the custom pattern →, takes you there.

A step has three levels, and a tap on it goes to the next one, round and round:

Level What the step does
Cut Lowers the signal by Depth: silence at 100%.
Half Halfway between a cut and the whole signal: at Depth 100% half the level, at 50% three quarters of it.
Pass Lets the signal through as it is.

Cut, half, pass, and back to cut: keep tapping a step until it shows the level you want.

  1. Tap the steps of the first row to set their levels. The bar of a step says its level, and so does its label, so you do not have to rely on the colour.

  2. Set the length with − and +: from 1 to 16 steps. Only the first steps are played; the dimmer ones after them are kept, so you can shorten a pattern and bring its end back.

  3. Set the steps per beat, from 1 to 8: with 2 a step is an eighth note, 4 a sixteenth, 3 a triplet, 1 a quarter note. The step then lasts 60 / (tempo × steps per beat × speed) seconds, as in the other patterns.
  4. Listen to it. Choosing Custom in the list plays it, and so does the first change you make to a step: Pattern goes to Custom, so what you write is what you hear. Where the editor has a page of its own, the Play this pattern button does the same without changing anything, and the arrows of the plugin and a device control assigned to Pattern also reach it.

Start from a built-in pattern

Copy from… copies one of the ten built-in patterns (steps, length and steps per beat) into your own, ready to be changed: the quickest way to get Gallop, but with a half step on the last note.

Your pattern is made of controls of the plugin, so it is saved with the pedalboard, with your own saved presets and with snapshots. The factory presets do not touch it. The settings have more than one page: use the arrows of the top bar (or swipe sideways) to go to the Saved presets. The settings page has everything the pedal has, and next to each control, a small button (the faders icon) that assigns it to a device control.

05

Playing it live

Every control of the plugin can be assigned to a device control (a footswitch, a knob, an expression pedal), the way you assign any parameter: open the settings of the plugin (the gear icon, or Edit pattern) and click the small button (the faders icon) next to the control to assign: On / off in the top bar, and Pattern, Tempo, Speed, Depth and Edge beside their names. The button fills in once the control is assigned.

Control Good to assign it to
Bypass A footswitch. In the dialog choose Momentary On to have the effect on only while you hold the footswitch (the kill switch of a guitar: you press, it chops; you let go, it is clean), or leave it as a toggle to turn it on and off with each press.
Pattern A knob, or a footswitch that goes through the patterns.
Tempo A knob, or an expression pedal.
Speed A footswitch: hold it for double speed, let go for normal.
Depth A knob or an expression pedal: from a gentle tremolo to a full cut.
Edge A knob: from a hard chop to a soft swell.

The plugin shows nothing on the device screen, so there is no pop-up to set up.

06

Factory presets

Open Saved presets in the settings of the plugin (or use the presets of the pedalboard) to pick one. Each one sets the pattern, the tempo, the speed, the depth and the edge; the bypass is not part of a preset.

All of them have the speed at 1x. The first four are named after a song and use a pattern in the style of its guitar part, at about its tempo; they are a starting point, not a copy.

07

Tips

Build your own from a built-in pattern

Pick the built-in pattern that is closest, Copy from… it into the custom pattern and change a step or two. Use the middle level for a ghost note: a step that is there, but soft.

Set the tempo to the song, then leave it

The patterns are in time with the tempo you set, not with the band. Adjust the number until the chops sit with the drums: a difference of one or two BPM is enough to drift off the beat over a bar.

Switch it on on the beat

The pattern restarts from its first step every time you switch the plugin on, and the built-in patterns start with a cut. Press the footswitch on the beat (or just before it) and the first chop lands exactly there.

Soften it with Depth

At 100% a cut is silence. At 40 to 60% the signal only dips, which sounds like a sharp tremolo, and fits a sound that should stay present (an ambient pad, a drive that you do not want to disappear).

Use Edge to change the character

Short edges (below 1 ms) are percussive: the sound is stopped as if a switch were flicked. Long edges (10 ms and more) turn the chop into a soft swell.

Put it where you want the cut

Before a delay, the cut chops what goes into the delay and the repeats go on ringing; after the delay, the repeats are chopped too. Try both places.

08

Questions & answers

Nothing is cut, I hear my guitar as it is.

Check that the label at the top of the plugin says On and the red light above the footswitch is lit. If it says Bypassed, click the footswitch. If the footswitch is assigned to a device control in Momentary mode, the effect is on only while you hold it.

The chops are not on the beat of my song.

The tempo is the plugin's own (section 3): set it by ear, or assign it to a knob. And switch the effect on on the beat: the pattern starts again from the beginning each time.

Does it add latency? Is it stereo?

No latency: the signal is only multiplied by a number that goes up and down. The plugin is mono: one audio input and one output. On a stereo pedalboard, put one on each side with the same pattern and tempo.

I hear a click at each cut.

Make Edge longer. At 0.1 ms the signal is stopped almost at once, which can click on a low note.

How many steps and how many levels can my own pattern have?

Up to 16 steps, each with three levels (cut, half and pass), at 1 to 8 steps per beat.

I edited my pattern and it did not change what I hear.

Check that Pattern is on Custom (the name on the plugin says so). The first edit switches it, but if you then chose another pattern with the arrows, or a controller did, choose Custom again in the list (or press Play this pattern). And the step must be inside the length: the dimmer steps after it are not played.

Is my pattern saved?

Yes, with the pedalboard, your saved presets and the snapshots. It is not in the factory presets, and it is not shared between pedalboards: each plugin on each pedalboard has its own.

Does it change the level of my sound when it is on?

Not while a step lets the signal through (it passes unchanged): the level only goes down in the cuts (and, a little, in the half steps). So there is nothing to compensate with a volume control.

Why are the patterns named after guitarists?

They are inspired by guitarists known for the kill switch, as a way to find the rhythm: the steps are our approximation of the style, not a transcription, and the plugin has no connection with the players or with their songs.

This manual is for version 1.0.9 of Kill Switch.
